correctness.rationale: For all Bernoulli parameters in [0,1], ex-ante EF means equal expected bundle sums. With 3 items, swapping the isolated item from b to a changes exact ex-post probability by c(a-b)[2-c-(1-c)(a+b-2ab)], which is nonnegative whenever a>=b, since 0<=a+b-2ab<=1. Splits dominate empty-versus-all because both one-sided weak-order probabilities dominate respective zero-count probabilities. This proves the universal boundary including endpoints. For the 4-item example, independent rational convolution and direct 256-outcome enumeration agree on the exact fractions and 12813853/12800000000 positive difference. The proof and code are mutually consistent, with no finite-to-infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The sharp 3/4 threshold is for the minimal unit-payoff Bernoulli family under heterogeneous item success rates. It reveals a structural failure of a natural ex-ante fairness heuristic without relying on unequal winning magnitudes or correlated agents. The three-good exchange identity classifies optimizers for all continuous parameter values. The specific gain is small, so only the qualitative sharp restriction and structural formula, not large performance loss, are claimed.
